chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat what falls from the food-spread, for it is a healing from every illness by the Permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for the one who wants to be healed by it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical benefit of eating food that falls from the table according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic tradition of minimizing waste and utilizing available resources for healing, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical wisdom in daily life. While often interpreted literally as a general remedy, scholars note it underscores the concept of 'shifa' (cure) being contingent upon divine permission and the purity of the consumed item. It serves as a reminder that sustenance, even in humble forms, carries spiritual and physical benefits when consumed with gratitude.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin yahya, form his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, form Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat what falls from the food-spread, for it is a healing from every illness by the Permission of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic for the one who wants to be healed by it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hassan ibn Rashid from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said,
’Eat what falls off of food, because in it is cure for all kinds of illness by the permission of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, for those who seek cures.’”
